title: arXiv Mathematics — notable papers in the 30 September 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred shortlist, and current citation/independent-attention evidence is too sparse to establish actual popularity.
ranking_note: Ordered by stated result scope, conjecture or problem status, quantitative advance, and recency—not measured readership or downloads.

sections.title: A negative answer to Erdős Problem #786
sections.abstract: Shows that admissible subsets of [1,N] cannot have density arbitrarily close to one and gives a logarithmic reciprocal-sum bound, answering both distinct-product questions negatively.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves Σ(1/a) ≤ (1/2) log N + (log log N + 2)^2 for every admissible A ⊆ [1,N], and |A| < (1−η)N for all sufficiently large N, for an absolute η>0; the paper reports Lean 4 formal verification.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Admissible means that equal products of distinct elements of A have the same number of factors on both sides; the cardinality bound is asymptotic in N.
sections.unique_caveat: The explicit density deficit is extremely small (η=e^-5000 is one allowed value); the optimal deficit is not determined.

sections.title: A nearly linear bound for the Lovász conjecture
sections.abstract: Improves the known guaranteed cycle length in an n-vertex connected vertex-transitive graph from n^(2/3−o(1)) to n^(1−o(1)).
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph on n vertices contains a cycle of length n^(1−o(1)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite, undirected, connected vertex-transitive graphs; the bound is asymptotic and is not a Hamiltonicity theorem.
sections.unique_caveat: The result falls short of a Hamiltonian path or cycle through all vertices, so the original Lovász conjecture remains unresolved.

sections.title: Asymptotics of the Brown–Erdős–Sós problem at integer exponents
sections.abstract: Determines the leading asymptotic coefficient for a broad integer-exponent family in sparse hypergraph Turán theory, with one even-parameter family left open.
sections.claimed_result: For f^(r)(n;(r−t)k+t,k), the authors establish the limit coefficient for every r>t≥2 except (r,t)=(3,2) with even k≥4; they give explicit formulas for odd k and for even k with r≥4, and prove a lower bound above 1/6 in the excluded family.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed integers r,k≥2 and r>t≥2, in the extremal problem for r-uniform hypergraphs avoiding k edges spanning at most (r−t)k+t vertices.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact coefficient remains unresolved for (r,t)=(3,2) and even k≥4; only a strict lower bound is obtained there.

sections.title: Proof of Fishburn’s latent-subset conjecture
sections.abstract: Proves Fishburn’s conjecture that every dual intersecting family has an index whose latent-subset family is at least as large as its corresponding star.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that for every dual intersecting F ⊆ 2^[n], some i∈[n] satisfies |F^L(i)| ≥ |F(i)|.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: F is a dual intersecting set family; F^L consists of subsets of members of F that are not themselves in F.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof uses the recent weighted star inequality of Chang, Liu, and Liu; this summary has not independently checked the proof or its use.

sections.title: Smyth’s Conjecture on the Mahler Measure of non-reciprocal trinomials of height 1
sections.abstract: Establishes Smyth’s conjectural threshold for Mahler measures of non-reciprocal trinomials of height 1 around ρ=M(x+y+1)=1.381356….
sections.claimed_result: The author determines exactly when the Mahler measure of a non-reciprocal height-1 trinomial is above or below ρ.
sections.unique_caveat: The extension from height-1 trinomials to the full sub-ρ spectrum for all non-reciprocal polynomials is described as conjectural.

sections.title: An infinite family of counterexamples to Goss’s conjecture on L-functions of cyclotomic function fields
sections.abstract: Constructs infinitely many counterexamples to Goss’s degree bound, with counterexample degrees growing as large as p−2.
sections.claimed_result: For q=p and P_a=T^p−T−a, the author derives deg_X g(X,ω_P^i)=n−1 for i=p^n−1; for p≥5 and 3≤n≤p−1 this contradicts Goss’s conjectured bound and reaches p−2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Cyclotomic function fields over F_p(T), with prime field size q=p and the specified irreducible polynomials and q-magic indices.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexamples are in the stated prime-field setting and do not settle analogous formulations for general prime powers q.

sections.title: Improved bounds on completion of partial Latin squares
sections.abstract: Raises the guaranteed completion threshold for partial Latin squares from a previous 0.08n bound to 0.231n filled cells per row, column, and symbol.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove completion when each row, column, and symbol occurs at most 0.231n times.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A partial Latin square of order n uses at most n symbols and has at most 0.231n filled cells for each symbol in each row and column; this is a sufficient condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The conjectured n/4 threshold remains unresolved; 0.231n is the sufficient bound proved in the abstract.
